text:
sandeep: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector change landed in staging, Mistral-7B sliding-window runs show weird tail latency spikes and a KV cache misalignment. Repro: long chat with dynamic max_pos override (1k->4k).
anya: ugh, saw that on a canary earlier. Can you paste the perf counters?
sandeep: basic numbers: p50 unchanged, p95 jumped from 120ms -> 360ms, token throughput down ~18%. Kernel-launch wait time up ~2.4x.
kevin: did we fallback to the scalar kernel accidentally for some windows?
sandeep: interesting — kernel-chooser logs show switching to 'tile_v2' for seq=1..512 then to 'fallback_sliding' for windows crossing 512->1024. The fallback path ends up re-copying KV slices.
zach: that copy is suspicious. Are we invalidating the KV view when RoPE scaling kicks in? M7b uses 32 heads/64dim per head here, we do RoPE rescale for max_pos override.
sandeep: profiler snippet (from perf-bot):
```
perf-bot: kernel_launchs: 1324 -> 3460; memcpy_bytes: 1.2GB -> 3.7GB; kernel_occupancy_low: 12% -> 8%
```
anya: memcpy increase confirms extra KV materialization. Could be due to our new kernel patch that assumes contiguous KV tiles, but sliding windows can create non-contig ranges.
kevin: also check seq_len_history used by batching heuristics — if we overestimate upcoming lengths we might be forcing large allocation/warmup and that affects throughput.
sandeep: I ran a small experiment disabling the new kernel-chooser heuristic (roll back to cost-based per-arch) and p95 returned to ~140ms. So chooser change is the proximate cause.
zach: but why does RoPE scaling affect it? Hypothesis: RoPE rescale code touches KV in-place to adjust positional factors and marks cache as "dirty" forcing re-serialize into tile-friendly buffer. When the chooser then picks fallback kernel it triggers the costly path.
anya: what about gating RoPE scaling until after kernel selection? i.e., compute which kernel we will use first, then apply rescale strategy that matches it. Might avoid the extra copy.
kevin: Proposed quick patch: add `kv_age` + `seq_window_pattern` to kernel cost model. If kv_age < threshold and windows are overlapping, bias towards non-copying kernels. Also make fallback path do lazy materialization (map view -> only copy if kernel actually needs contiguous layout).
sandeep: I sketched a patch:
```
// pseudo
if (needs_contiguous && !kv_view.can_be_contiguous()) {
  if (!kernel_requires_copy) choose_kernel_that_works_with_view();
  else lazy_copy_on_first_use();
}
```
kevin: +1 for lazy_copy_on_first_use. Also add a telemetry tag `kv_materialized=true/false` per request so we can correlate with perf.
perf-bot: correlation check completed: requests with kv_materialized=true had p95 2.8x higher on staging for sliding-window traces. (n=420)
zach: sweet — that telemetry proves it. Let's do small A/B: enable lazy copy in A, leave B as-is for 6h on canary. Collect p50/p95, memcpy.
anya: also add an internal unit test: simulate overlapping windows with RoPE rescale (max_pos override) and assert kernel chooser does not trigger copy path. Keep test lightweight.
sandeep: created a draft PR with chooser tweak + telemetry, link: https://rwd.in/pr/1234 (please review)
kevin: will review now. One more ask: update batching heuristics to consider `seq_overlap_ratio` so we don't overbatch sequences that will cause cross-window fallbacks. Maybe reduce max_batch_size for high overlap workloads.
zach: agreed. I can prototype an estimator that looks at recent request sequence vectors and computes overlap ratio cheaply.
anya: follow-ups: 1) land lazy copy + telemetry, 2) run A/B on canary, 3) add unit + e2e reproducer, 4) consider batching tweak if A/B still shows regression.
sandeep: thanks. I'll mark this as high-priority for today's runtime squad triage. @kevin @anya @zach ping when reviews landed. :thumbsup:
